status_definitions.STATICALLY_RESOLVED: Enough static/deterministic evidence exists that no runtime observation is required for this bounded question.
status_definitions.STATICALLY_SOLVABLE: Not solved yet, but concrete static avenues remain (named files/functions/techniques); never placed in the runtime backlog.
status_definitions.STATICALLY_AMBIGUOUS: Extensive static work has narrowed the possibilities to two or more remaining interpretations; runtime may eventually be needed only after the relevant static graph is exhausted.
status_definitions.RUNTIME_ESSENTIAL: The answer fundamentally depends on dynamic information no static evidence can supply.

questions.question: What do xdbboxr.adf header words 0 and 1 represent, and are they consumed by executable code?
questions.evidence: CORRECTED by follow-up static RE. word0=121 is the field/column count, not the boxer-record count. func_001ACCAC bounds field_id against word0 and func_001AD268 scans exactly word0 packed 2-bit field-type entries. word1=37 is the base-table record count: func_001AD21C returns word1 and func_001AD180 bounds record_index against it, then computes the selected row using stride word0*2. The old interpretation of 121 as a per-boxer record count is superseded.

questions.question: What is xdbboxr.adf's exact per-record field layout (name, rating, weight, division, stance, handedness, appearance, hair, shorts, hometown, career-eligibility, rivals, training, store-unlock, created-boxer data)?
questions.evidence: The generic XDB layout is resolved far enough to map concrete boxer fields. xdbboxr.adf has a 24-byte header, 121 fields, 37 base records, a 31-byte 2-bit-per-field type map at +0x18, and a row-major token matrix at +0x38 with 0xF2-byte rows. Generic accessors prove type 0=inline signed int16, type 1=string/byte pool, type 2=int32 pool, type 3=float pool. UpdateSelectBoxerInfo at 0x001D53F0 maps Power fields 0x10/0x11, Speed 0x12, Agility 0x13, Stamina 0x14, Chin 0x15, Heart 0x16, Cuts 0x17 and Body 0x18; iOverall is computed by func_001D50F4. Name composition resolves field 1=surname/family name and field 2=first/given name; field 3 is a short CRO/resource stem. CORRECTION: field 0 is not the global SelectBoxer/fight-session boxer selector. func_00186284 proves that selector is a cumulative record-position index across registered boxer tables and never consults field 0; rows 35/36 are selected as indices 35/36 even though their field-0 values are 74/75. Field 0 is therefore a secondary/resource identity number with exact role still unresolved. Field 4 is the base/default availability flag: func_00185D84 returns field4>0, the 35-entry stock-list builder consumes that predicate, and func_001B0FE8 falls back to a +0x1C4 unlock bitset for selector 35 when field4 is zero. Field 6 is a confirmed hometown foreign-key into xdbhmtwn.adf; field 7 is a confirmed nickname/alias foreign-key into xdbalias.adf; field 9 is the confirmed boxer-weight field used by the exact six-division classifier. Compact helpers also expose field 0x0D as high-byte+1900 plus low-byte components and field 0x0E as three nibble components, but those packed semantics are not yet named. Two further boxer fields are now confirmed through cross-table accessor chains. Field 0x06 is the xdbhmtwn.adf record ID: T_00185FA0/T_001860A0 read boxer field 6, enter the hometown accessor path at func_001A9020, and retrieve hometown record fields; decoded references land within the 63-record hometown table and expose O_Home_* localization keys. Field 0x07 is the xdbalias.adf nickname record ID: func_00185F34/T_00186108 read boxer field 7, enter the alias accessor path at func_00185008, and retrieve alias fields; decoded references land within the 76-record alias table and expose ST_Nick_* keys. Field 0x0F is also behaviorally resolved: func_001857E4 reads it as a mode gate. When zero, the game's displayed/effective rating path scales rating fields 0x10-0x18 through the boxer's weight class and D_FLT_0055E280 before clamping to 10..100; when nonzero, the alternate path uses the raw/base rating accessor and clamps directly. T_00187434/func_00187548 take complementary branches on this flag. All 37 tracked base rows currently store zero, so the exact boxer category/source that sets a nonzero value remains open. Field 0x05 is now resolved one level further and a prior speech/audio classification is corrected. func_00185B30 reads field 0x05; func_0010C9C8 uses it as a bounded 76-entry source selector and returns a normalized boxer code, with a fallback through field 0x07's alias-linked path for unmapped cases. func_0010BB58 runs that normalizer for both active boxers, writes the two results into payload offsets +0x14/+0x18, and dispatches the payload through func_003E5860. On first-use failure it registers/resolves descriptor D_0055AB38 via func_003E4A94; that descriptor is named 'Replay'. Therefore field 0x05 is proven to feed boxer identity/profile codes into the Replay event path. It is not proven to be a commentary/speech/audio ID.
questions.remaining_static_work: Mapped so far: name/resource fields 0x00-0x03; base availability 0x04; Replay-event identity selector 0x05; hometown 0x06; nickname/alias 0x07; weight 0x09/division classifier; packed career timing 0x0D; packed trait components 0x0E; rating-mode behavior 0x0F; ratings 0x10-0x18; stance 0x19; style 0x1A; skin tone and several head-appearance fields 0x34-0x39; hair-style resource token 0x71. Continue with physical/biographical fields 0x08/0x0A-0x0C, exact 0x0E trait names, remaining handedness/equipment, career/store and created-boxer semantics. The exact authored name/downstream interpretation of the normalized Replay code remains open but must not be conflated with commentary.

questions.question: What does func_00186464's 8-bit-masked linked-list index actually select (boxer record vs. table-instance registration)?
questions.evidence: RESOLVED during Overhaul Alpha 1's targeted static RE (analysis/resources/overhaul-alpha1-evidence.json entry alpha1-03). func_0018654C (a caller of func_00186464 flagged since the first boxer-schema pass) was disassembled in full: it walks func_186464(0), func_186464(1), ... via the proven 8-bit index until null, calling an INDIRECT FUNCTION POINTER read from a per-node vtable-like sub-table for each node (the same {i16,funcptr} shape already proven for the generic resource-table loader), then appends its own caller-supplied object onto the list's end by writing the found node's +0x10 'next' field (node->0x10 = new_object; new_object->0xC = node -- the previously-missing list-insertion writer). This is a table-instance REGISTRY append/measure pattern over heterogeneous nodes each queried via its own function pointer -- not a homogeneous boxer-record array. Boxer records are proven (program-04-02) to be indexed via xdbboxr.adf's own header word0 through func_001AD268, a completely separate mechanism. The 'table-instance registration' interpretation is confirmed; the 'boxer record' interpretation is ruled out.

questions.question: Is there a fixed maximum roster/boxer-database record count?
questions.evidence: The former 121-entry roster-cap hypothesis is disproven: 121 is xdbboxr.adf's field_count, while word1=37 is its base record_count and is read dynamically by func_001AD21C/func_001AD180. func_00186284 proves the boxer selector used by fight/session/UI code is a cumulative record-position index across registered boxer table instances: it subtracts each table's dynamic record_count and passes the residual index to func_001AD180. It does not lookup xdbboxr field 0. Normal stock SelectBoxer ranges cover selector indices 0-34; physical base rows 35 and 36 are Fabolous and Little Mac. Their field-0 values are 74/75, proving only that field 0 is a separate secondary identity/resource key, not that their selector indices are 74/75. No fixed total roster maximum is established.
questions.remaining_static_work: Trace the created/custom-boxer table/save path and any independent allocation/serialization consumer that could impose a fixed cap across the cumulative registered-table selector space. Determine field 0's secondary/resource-ID role separately; do not use it as the roster selector.
questions.confidence: CONFIRMED for dynamic cumulative selector mechanics; fixed total maximum remains open.

questions.question: Does fnhud.hud's format expose named field bindings for stamina, health, damage, stun, knockdowns, rounds, timers, scorecards, judges, or boxer slots (relevant to programs 05/07/08/10/11's in-fight HUD data)?
questions.evidence: fnhud.hud (33,528 bytes) is NOT a BIGF archive -- it has the custom binary header already noted in the prior pass's backlog (magic bytes 01 00 f4 f1), now partially decoded: a repeating sequence of what appear to be (size, type_id, offset) u32 triples immediately following the 16-byte magic/version prefix. This delta pass extracted its full ASCII string content (151 unique runs) and found it is NOT a text-field-binding format the way the .apt/.const UI packages are -- it consists of short, tagged component/geometry-piece identifiers (4-character codes such as RN01-RN15, RC01-RC21, RCH1-RCH5, CM01-CM17, CD01-CD10, MH01-MH17, OL01-OL12, OV01-OV08, PU01-PU15, CY01-CY03, plus rendering-primitive keywords POLY/fill/flre/blnk/load/LINE). These read as a component-indexed vector-HUD-geometry container (glyph/digit/icon pieces for on-screen HUD rendering), not a semantic field-binding table like the .apt/.const files. Per this project's explicit discipline, no field semantics are inferred from these 4-character labels alone (e.g. 'RN' plausibly maps to round-number digit glyphs and 'RC' to round-card pieces, but this is not asserted as proven) -- this corrects the assumption that fnhud.hud would directly expose gameplay field names the way selectboxer.big/optionsettings.big did.
questions.remaining_static_work: Fully decode fnhud.hud's header table structure (the repeating size/type/offset triples) to establish an authoritative component hierarchy, then determine whether any component ties back to a BOOT.BIN-owned numeric field (e.g. via a renderer-consumer function) rather than inferring meaning from the 4-character tags alone.

questions.question: Beyond the already-proven '3-knockdown rule', does the retail options menu expose other named, distinct damage/stoppage rule toggles (auto-recovery, KO moment/highlight, fight stoppage, illegal blows, saved-by-the-bell)?

The underlying native accessor family is GetOptionsSettings/SetOptionsSettings. func_001D9958/func_001DC52C/func_001FB6B8 decode a packed 32-bit settings word at fight-session offset +0x15C. FOLLOW-UP cross-build RE corrects an earlier interpretation: +0x19A8 is not another options bitfield. func_001AFFDC writes it as a bounded fight/session mode enum (valid signed values <9, otherwise -1), and the debug quick-fight path writes mode 1. func_001D9958 uses +0x19A8 as a mode gate while decoding/serving options. Offset +0x1955 remains a separate byte flag/gate. Thus the retail options storage remains bit-packed at +0x15C, while +0x19A8 selects context/mode-dependent behavior.

questions.question: Do per-judge weighting differences (e.g. 'generous' vs. 'strict' judges) exist statically?

T_001F7248 (the real GetJudgesScoreInfo implementation, confirmed real by its 216-instruction size) was disassembled in full: it fetches three judge-object handles via func_01ED5C(context, judge_index) for judge_index in {0,1,2} (independently proving TOTAL_JUDGES==3, matching judgesscores.big!judgesScores.const's own TOTAL_JUDGES constant), then applies an IDENTICAL call shape (same func_08A02C/func_08A00C calls, same argument pattern) to each of the three handles -- CONFIRMED: no differential weighting exists in this calling code. What remains open: func_08A02C's own body (not disassembled this pass) could still apply a per-judge-object internal bias baked into each judge handle's own state; that narrower sub-question is why this entry remains STATICALLY_AMBIGUOUS rather than fully resolved.

Exact branches are: weight <127 -> Featherweight (enum 5); 127-135 -> Lightweight (4); 136-147 -> Welterweight (3); 148-168 -> Middleweight (2); 169-190 -> Light Heavyweight (1); 191-280 -> Heavyweight (0); >=281 -> invalid/-1.
